description: Advisories from `composer audit --locked` that this fork knowingly carries.
The gate (scripts/ci/composer-audit.sh) fails on any advisory NOT listed
here. That is the point: none of these versions is this fork's choice —
app/composer.json is upstream's bluespice/core and every affected package is
a transitive dependency of MediaWiki 1.43.9 / BlueSpice 5.1.9, or a vendored
extension of it — so a bare audit would be red on every push and would be
ignored within a week. What is worth failing a push over is a NEW advisory,
and that is what this comparison detects.
Entries marked ACTION REQUIRED are fixable, but only by re-vendoring an
upstream tree, which is docs/dev/upgrade-runbook.md, not a PR. Read them
at the start of every upgrade: they are the reason to take one.
This file cannot see: MediaWiki core (vendored source, not a composer
package — that is the release-watch job, Track B), the two frozen packages
(stripped from composer.lock — Track C, see VERSIONS.yml and SECURITY.md),
or any vendored extension that is not also a composer package.

guzzlehttp/guzzle.why:
Pinned to exactly 7.12.3 by upstream's app/composer.json (bluespice/core); wikimedia/shellbox is the only runtime requirer and asks for ^7.9.2, so this is not a version this fork picks. Guzzle is also the transport behind MediaWiki core's HttpRequestFactory (app/includes/http/GuzzleHttpRequest.php), which is a wider surface than the shellbox-only framing this entry used to carry. Every advisory below is fixed past 7.12.3, so all six move together when upstream repins — none is closable here.

FOUR MEDIUMS, carried since the 1.43.9 / 5.1.9 upgrade cleared six of the ten this package used to have, and none with a CVE: URI fragments disclosed in redirect Referer headers, host-only cookie scope not preserved, unbounded response cookies, and Proxy-Authorization headers forwarded to origin servers. Fixed in 7.14.2 and 7.15.1.

CVE-2026-69246 (high, CVSS 7.2, fixed in 7.15.2), new 2026-08. Guzzle hands the URI to the transport while supplying Host separately, and libcurl decodes a percent-encoded host — 127.0.0.%31 — that the application's own check saw literally, so a host allowlist, denylist or private-range check can be evaded. It needs the application both to build URIs from untrusted input and to host-validate before handing off, and this tree has no such check to evade: $wgAllowCopyUploads is left at core's default (off) and no $wgCopyUploadsDomains is set anywhere in app/settings.d/. ExternalData is loaded (app/settings.d/040-BlueSpiceProDistribution.php:70) with AllowGetters at its default true, so an editor can already point {{#get_web_data:}} at any host — that is unrestricted SSRF by configuration, which this CVE neither creates nor worsens. Re-review this paragraph the day a host allowlist is introduced, because that is the configuration the CVE is about.

CVE-2026-69245 (medium, CVSS 6.5, fixed in 7.15.2), new 2026-08. SetCookie::matchesDomain() validates before canonicalising, so hex, octal and percent-escaped IP literals keep subdomain scope they should not (CWE-180). Not reachable here: core removes Guzzle's cookie middleware outright and substitutes its own MediaWiki CookieJar (app/includes/http/GuzzleHttpRequest.php:171), so matchesDomain() is not on the path for any core-originated request. The advisory also notes that no public DNS delegation yields such a name, which confines it to private networks and container environments.

mediawiki/semantic-media-wiki.why:
ACTION REQUIRED, and still open as a version: 8 advisories against vendored 6.0.1, none closable by re-vendoring in this tree. Verified fix-version mapping (packagist security-advisories API + GitHub Advisory API first_patched_version, cross-checked against upstream RELEASE-NOTES-7.{0.0,2.0,2.1,3.0}.md, 2026-09-23): CVE-2025-61682 / GHSA-hg8h-557g-q8pp (high, stored XSS via a non-reserved data-* attribute) fixed in 7.0.0; CVE-2026-77606 / GHSA-3jp5-3h47-28qf, CVE-2026-77607 / GHSA-7xv3-gf2g-498h, CVE-2026-77608 / GHSA-59xw-qv23-j3rc, CVE-2026-77609 / GHSA-hw3m-8j5x-94ff, CVE-2026-77610 / GHSA-q5fm-9mx6-44f4 (all medium) fixed in 7.2.0; GHSA-9rcc-pmj8-ffhr (medium, no CVE) fixed in 7.2.1; GHSA-jr78-w6w5-m8f8 (`action=smwtask`, high, no CVE, unauthenticated) fixed in 7.3.0. The minimum version closing all 8 is 7.3.0.

BLOCKED, twice over, same class as mediawiki/maps below. (1) app/_bluespice/build/bluespice-pro-distribution/composer.json:53 constrains mediawiki/semantic-media-wiki to 6.0.*, merged into the root resolver constraints by wikimedia/composer-merge-plugin via app/composer.local.json. (2) even with that relaxed, resolution fails on an empty intersection: bluespice/foundation@5.1.9 requires param-processor/param-processor 1.12.*, SMW 7.3.0 requires ~1.13 — closing it means forking bluespice/foundation's own composer.json, not a scoped re-vendor. Both constraints are upstream BlueSpice's, not this fork's; only a BlueSpice series bump (a milestone, not a phase — see Phase 6 of ROADMAP.md, DEPS-02) relaxes either. Full derivation: .planning/features/deps02-smw-revendor/PLAN.md §2-§3 (gitignored, not in this diff).

MITIGATED IN TREE as of 2026-09-23, 7 of the 8: upstream fixes backported as Class A patches — smw-ask-sep-xss (CVE-2026-77607), smw-ask-plain-header-xss (CVE-2026-77606), smw-searchbyproperty-error-xss (CVE-2026-77608), smw-uriresolver-open-redirect (CVE-2026-77609), smw-debug-query-xss (CVE-2026-77610), smw-facetedsearch-cstate-xss (GHSA-9rcc-pmj8-ffhr), and the smw-subtab-xss pair (CVE-2025-61682) — see docs/dev/patches.md. Class A: composer reinstalls the package on every run and docker/setup.sh re-applies them via scripts/apply-patches.sh --class A; scripts/verify-patches.sh is what catches it if that ever stops happening.

CARRIED, mitigation scheduled elsewhere: GHSA-jr78-w6w5-m8f8 (`action=smwtask`, high) grants unauthenticated access to admin-only maintenance operations and internal database statistics — the one unauthenticated-reachable advisory of the 8, and deliberately not backported here. It is handed off to the ChatBot Sibling Handler Sweep (Phase 7), which is already building the anon-request-refused T3 machinery this needs; that phase's ROADMAP entry and SEC-06's requirement text name it as inherited scope. Until it lands there, this one advisory stays unmitigated.

The entry stays and the marker stays because the installed version is still 6.0.1 — composer audit is reporting the truth, and a patched tree is not the same as a fixed dependency. Re-vendoring to 7.3.0 remains the real fix (recorded as a BlueSpice-series-bump milestone candidate); when it lands, delete this entry and all nine SMW patches together.

Upstream report (AC8): the 6.0.* pin and the param-processor 1.12.* constraint behind it have not yet been filed with BlueSpice as of this commit — that is an orchestrator-owned action (no live upstream-facing reporting from this implementer session); record the reference here once filed.

mediawiki/maps.why:
ACTION REQUIRED, and still open as a version: the 1.43.9 / 5.1.9 upgrade did not move Maps and cannot. CVE-2026-52854 (high) is stored XSS through the layers and overlays parameters of the display_map parser function, fixed upstream in 12.1.3; this tree vendors 11.0.1 at app/extensions/Maps and app/_bluespice/build/bluespice-pro-distribution/composer.json:36 constrains mediawiki/maps to 11.0.*, so only a BlueSpice series bump relaxes it. Any editor who can save wikitext can reach the parser function, which made this the most exposed entry in this file.

MITIGATED IN TREE as of 2026-08-04, but deliberately still listed. Upstream commit 737a993f (released in 12.1.3) is backported as two Class A patches, maps-layercontrol-xss-php and maps-layercontrol-xss-js — see docs/dev/patches.md. The PHP half filters layers and overlays to the egMapsLeafletAvailableLayers / egMapsLeafletAvailableOverlayLayers whitelists that ParamProcessor only warned about, so a hostile value never reaches the client; the JS half escapes both places Leaflet renders a name as a layer-control label. Class A means composer reinstalls the package over them on every run and docker/setup.sh re-applies them; scripts/verify-patches.sh is what catches it if that ever stops happening.

The entry stays and the marker stays because the installed version is still 11.0.1 — composer audit is reporting the truth, and a patched tree is not the same as a fixed dependency. Re-vendoring to 12.1.3 remains the real fix; when it lands, delete this entry and both patches together.

squizlabs/php_codesniffer.why: Dev-only transitive dependency (packages-dev) pulled in by mediawiki/mediawiki-codesniffer v45.0.0, which pins it to exactly 3.10.3. Neither check.sh nor .gitlab-ci.yml invokes phpcs — the tool ships in the lockfile but is never executed by any gate or runtime image. The advisory (CVE-2026-67434, high, OS command injection, fixed in 3.13.6) cannot be reached without deliberately running phpcs against hostile input, which this fork does not do. Clearing it would require bumping mediawiki-codesniffer from v45 to v52 (the only version shipping phpcs 3.13.6), a jump that also requires PHP 8.3 and pulls in new coding-standard rules — disproportionate for a tool this fork does not invoke.

web-auth/webauthn-lib.why: Low, and specific to SimpleFakeCredentialGenerator used with an empty secret — a username-enumeration hardening feature, not an authentication bypass. The upgrade moved this 4.9.2 → 4.9.3, which does not clear it: the advisory covers >=4.9.0,<5.3.5 and mediawiki/web-authn requires ^4.9.2, so the fix is a major bump upstream has not taken. Not this fork's version to choose.
